purpose: library: ocean acidification as acid-base chemistry — a reduction in ocean pH from uptake of atmospheric CO2; more than 200 years of rising atmospheric CO2 from fossil-fuel burning and land-use change; the ocean absorbing about 30 percent of released CO2; the series of chemical reactions that raise hydrogen-ion concentration (more acidic seawater) and make carbonate ions relatively less abundant; carbonate ions as the building block of shells and coral skeletons; the resulting difficulty for calcifying organisms (oysters, clams, sea urchins, shallow and deep sea corals, calcareous plankton); effects on non-calcifying organisms (fish predator detection) and the food web. Fits quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the 30-percent and 200-year figures, step ordering of the cause→reaction→effect chain, and a concept map.
